report.title: Gulf of Mexico well permits by rig type: a public US data file

code.install: none: the counting script uses the standard library

inputs.description: BSEE Application for Permit to Drill raw data: permit type, requested spud date, water depth, rig name and rig type
inputs.source: US Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement, BSEE Data Center
inputs.version_or_date: page counts: file of 2 November 2026; eval: file of the run date

inputs.description: BSEE Incident Investigations raw data; the pinned counting script reads it as well, although the permit counts do not use it
inputs.source: US Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement, BSEE Data Center

inputs.description: Published Figure 1 data: new-well permits by year and rig type

missing_data.what: The APD file of 2 November 2026 (SHA-256 b4ab6606...)
missing_data.why: BSEE replaces the file daily and does not keep old copies.
missing_data.how_to_supply: Not needed while today's file gives the same counts; the published Figure 1 CSV holds the counted values.
missing_data.effect: A later file can differ by a few permits; the eval reports that as drift.

missing_data.what: The counting script on the main branch of worldenergydata
missing_data.why: The pinned commit is on a branch that is not merged yet.
missing_data.how_to_supply: Not needed: the eval reads the script from the pinned commit of any clone (it fetches the commit if needed).
missing_data.effect: Step 1 fetches the pinned commit by its SHA, or else through refs/pull/1844/head, which GitHub keeps after the branch is deleted, so the pin stays fetchable after a squash merge. A candidate run needs the script on main.

cannot_do: Say which rig actually drilled each well: the file names the rig type of the permit.
Rebuild the exact file of 2 November 2026: BSEE does not archive daily copies.
